logline: A 1986 detective chasing a serial killer through a tunnel reappears 30 years later in 2016, forced to partner with modern investigators as the same killer's pattern resurfaces.

renewal.note: Single-season run of 16 episodes concluded on May 21, 2017. The series became the highest-rated drama in OCN history at that point. Thai and Indonesian remakes followed.

bollymeter.basis: IMDb 8.2 and a record-breaking OCN ratings run; critics positioned it among the best non-romantic K-dramas alongside Beyond Evil and Stranger, praising its victim-centred storytelling and the procedural craft of its time-slip mechanics.

seasons.review_body: Tunnel premiered on OCN in March 2017 with a 2.8 percent cable rating and built steadily to set a new all-time record for the network. The series distinguishes itself from the crowded time-travel K-drama field by anchoring its procedural mechanics in the emotional weight of cold-case grief - the suffering of victims' families is foregrounded in ways that push it above genre exercise. Choi Jin-hyuk's performance as the 1986 detective disoriented by modern Seoul balances fish-out-of-water comedy against genuine procedural tension. Audience commentary on IMDb (8.2) places it in the upper tier of Korean crime dramas; its comparison set on fan rankings runs alongside Stranger and Signal. The first four episodes build slowly, but the midpoint payoff justifies the setup.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The 1986 cold open establishes the serial-killer case with genuine procedural weight before the time-slip device launches the series' central conceit; the tonal control is notable for a cable crime thriller.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The detective emerging from the tunnel into 2016 Seoul - the show's central image, handled with restraint rather than spectacle.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 16
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale resolves the killer's identity and the detective's temporal paradox with an emotional precision that matched the show's best episodes; the victim-centred closure felt earned rather than neat.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The revelation that reframes the personal stakes of the entire investigation.
